cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Stay for the Hard Part
cards.instruction: Create increasing moments of emotional honesty to test whether someone remains present and supportive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll clear this up before we go back into the reunion. I wasn't just late.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I saved you a seat beside me. Was it the traffic?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. I waited outside for half an hour. I'll come back in with you, but hear me first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm listening. I thought you didn't want to sit with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wanted that seat. I was afraid you'd be happier without me. Will you take me to it?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 directs clearing things up before return; A3 offers going in with B to retain a hearing; A5 reveals fear of being unwanted and needs B accompaniment.

responseLogic.evidence: A1 establishes a conversation outside the reunion now; A3 earlier waiting and B2 saved seat explain the lateness without a specific traffic backstory.

relationship.evidence: B2 asks why A missed the saved seat; B4 remains listening while admitting personal hurt.

heightening.evidence: B4 thought A did not want proximity; A5 reveals the inverse fear and asks to be taken to the seat.

specificity.evidence: A1 reunion return and B2 seat establish setting and attachment; A3 clarifies the half-hour avoidance.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 wanted seat, fear and accompaniment request each do necessary interpersonal work; no abstract account of honesty remains.
